name: Pulmonary Atresia with Intact Ventricular Septum Syndrome
aliases: Pulmonary Atresia with Intact Interventricular Septum

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and Cardiac Catheterization Diagnostic Criteria for PA-IVS

criteria.description: Complete atresia of the pulmonary valve with no antegrade flow from the right ventricle to the pulmonary artery
Absence of ventricular septal defect confirmed by imaging
Hypoplastic or small right ventricle with variable degrees of right ventricular-coronary artery fistulas
Dependence on patent ductus arteriosus for pulmonary blood flow

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pulmonary valve atresia with intact ventricular septum and right ventricular hypoplasia confirmed by echocardiography or cardiac catheterization
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is typically made prenatally or in the neonatal period using echocardiography and confirmed by cardiac catheterization.

laboratory: Elevated hematocrit due to secondary polycythemia
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating pulmonary valve atresia and intact ventricular septum
Cardiac catheterization confirming right ventricular morphology and coronary artery fistulas
Chest X-ray showing decreased pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence
Rare associations with chromosomal abnormalities in some cases
other: Dependence on prostaglandin E1 infusion to maintain ductus arteriosus patency in neonates

distinguishingFeatures: Right ventricular outflow tract obstruction but not complete atresia

redFlags: Severe neonatal cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Dependence on prostaglandin E1 to maintain ductal patency
Signs of right heart failure or shock in the neonatal period
references: Anderson RH, et al. Paediatric Cardiology. 4th ed. Churchill Livingstone; 2010.
Moller JH, et al. The Atlas of Congenital Heart Disease and Surgery. 2nd ed. Futura Publishing; 2000.
